messages:
anya: Heads-up — after rolling the preemptive soft-slotting change to canary yesterday, we saw 2 small OOMs and a notable tail-latency spike on a few 2k+ token requests. Trying to collect context here :eyes:
jack: ugh. which change exactly? the preemptive queue rebalancer that moves partial batches across slots?
sree: yep that one. it will try to rebalance queued items to reduce idle slots and improve batching density. saw perf improvement on microbenchmarks but not across live traces.
anya: attaching quick snippet from the agent logs that correlated with the OOMs:
anya: ```
[2026-02-14T05:12:43Z] evictor: headroom low (available_kv=120MB, min_reserved=256MB)
[2026-02-14T05:12:43Z] preemptive_slotter: moved 3 requests to slot-7 (total_tokens=4200)
[2026-02-14T05:12:43Z] batch_assembler: admitted batch size 6, token_budget_exceeded -> fallback to kernel-fallback
[2026-02-14T05:12:44Z] gpu_driver: cudamem OOM on allocate 340MB
```
maria: interesting — moved 3 rqs with 4.2k tokens into one slot? that seems like a bad packing choice when kv footprint is high.
jack: what's the current token_budget target for preemptive-slotting? i thought we clipped at 2k per slot by default.
sree: preemptive-slotter uses a dynamic budget: target per-slot = max(800, min(2500, median_queue_tok * 1.6)) — the idea was to adapt to traffic, but it only considers request token counts, not live KV usage.
anya: right — it ignored per-slot kv_pressure metric. we have high shared KV footprint on some models (long context + cached activations) so two big requests in same slot kills headroom.
jack: can we short-circuit the rebalancer to consult kv_free_bytes before moving? something like: if kv_free < kv_reserve_threshold then no cross-slot merge.
sree: that's one approach. also thinking about introducing a "soft-safety" tag: when slot is tagged high-kv, limit merged_token_budget to 50% of normal. simple and cheap.
maria: do we have profiling that shows kernel selection being impacted? batch assembler might pick a faster kernel for larger batch + short seq, but with KV-induced memory fragmentation the chosen kernels allocate and fail.
anya: i profiled one canary pod with heap snapshots — fragmentation + pinned KV pages meant large contiguous GPU allocs failed even though total free looked borderline ok. kernel selection wants contiguous workspace.
jack: so two orthogonal problems: admission/batching logic that ignores KV pressure, and kernel allocator fragility under fragmentation. both caused the OOM cascade.
sree: propose short term mitigations: 1) short-circuit rebalancer when kv_free_bytes < 300MB, 2) clamp merged_token_budget to 1.2x median instead of 1.6x for slots with any cached KV entries, 3) prefer conservative kernels when kv_fragmentation_flag=true.
maria: agree. also add a canary metric: preemptive_moves_per_min and preemptive_moves_failed_allocs to see correlation.
ops-bot: deploy-plan created: canary=5% cluster, feature_flag=soft-slotting-kv-guard, rollout=gradual 3 steps, alert-on=oom_rate_up50pct.
anya: implemented quick guard locally, results look promising — no OOMs in 6h. tail p99 latency reduced back to baseline.
jack: nice. next: for medium term we should make the batch admission model kv-aware end-to-end — admission should consider estimated kv_bytes_per_token (model-profiled) * tokens_in_batch in its headroom calc.
sree: agreed. I'll add a task to inference runtime backlog: "kv-aware admission scoring + kernel fallback heuristics" with profiling subtask to collect kv_bytes_per_token per model.
maria: I'll add dashboards and alerts for the new metrics. add sample query: `sum by(pod) (preemptive_moves_failed_allocs) / sum by(pod) (preemptive_moves)` to flag high failure rate.
anya: ok let's revert canary to stable if no regressions in 24h, keep the guard flag on until the kv-aware admission lands. thanks all :thumbsup:
jack: great writeup — left a couple inline comments on the PR.
sree: thanks, i'll push the kv param collection job today.
anya: closing loop later with perf numbers. if anyone sees odd OOMs please ping me @anya immediately.
